public_rationale: DORA describes time saved writing with AI being spent auditing its output [e1]. The item discusses general AI adoption, without pairing a documented token-consumption reward policy with measured software-quality and maintenance outcomes [e1]. It therefore establishes neither inevitable poor software under such rewards nor a verified counterexample [e1].
limitations: The evidence does not isolate token-consumption rewards from general AI adoption or other engineering practices [e1].
Reported verification costs do not establish poor software quality or maintenance; the item provides no longitudinal audit of those outcomes under a token-reward policy [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Companies that reward token consumption guarantee their software will be poorly written and maintained.

statement.excerpt: They are guaranteeing that their software will be poorly-written and maintained, all in the pursuit of “doing more AI” for no reason other than that everybody else appears to be doing so.
statement.document_title: The AI Industry Is Lying To You

from_speaker: Companies incentivizing the amount of tokens you burn
our_interpretation: The claim concerns rewarding token consumption, rather than merely providing AI coding tools.
The ordinary reading of 'guaranteeing' is that these incentives necessarily produce poor software quality and maintenance.
Poor quality means material defects, reliability problems or maintainability problems assessed against ordinary engineering standards.
criteria.support_condition: Audits and credible causal comparisons establish that rewarding token consumption necessarily produces poor code and maintenance. Examples of defective AI-generated code alone are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented company rewards token consumption while independently verified software quality and maintenance remain good, providing a counterexample to the guarantee.

evidence.excerpt: Time saved writing is often re-spent auditing.
evidence.locator: The hidden taxes of AI adoption; subsection 1, The verification tax
evidence.explanation: The analysis draws on Google engineers' 2025 survey responses and identifies verification costs. It does not isolate rewards for token consumption or establish inevitable poor maintenance.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Documented token-consumption reward policies paired with independent measurements of defects and maintenance over time, with causal comparisons separating policy effects from staffing, review practices and project complexity. Support requires establishing necessity, rather than isolated failures. A documented company rewarding token consumption while independently verified software quality and maintenance remain good would contradict the guarantee.
